TypeSignature.Value: .class public auto ansi sealed SKDifferenceStyle extends System.Enum

Docs.summary: Opaque diagnostic representations of a decoded pixel comparison.

MemberSignature.Value: .field public static literal valuetype SkiaSharp.Testing.SKDifferenceStyle BinaryMask = int32(0)

Docs.summary: Mismatched pixels are white; all other pixels, including ignored coverage, are black, using the same predicate as the comparison.

MemberSignature.Value: .field public static literal valuetype SkiaSharp.Testing.SKDifferenceStyle ChannelDifference = int32(1)

Docs.summary: Raw absolute RGB channel differences, including disabled RGB channels; ignored pixels are black and alpha differences are never represented.

MemberSignature.Value: .field public static literal valuetype SkiaSharp.Testing.SKDifferenceStyle Heatmap = int32(4)

Docs.summary: Largest raw absolute selected-channel difference on a fixed 0-255 scale: black at zero, then blue through cyan and yellow to red; ignored pixels are gray (128,128,128).
Docs.remarks: Tolerances do not suppress magnitudes. Output alpha is always 255.

MemberSignature.Value: .field public static literal valuetype SkiaSharp.Testing.SKDifferenceStyle ThresholdMap = int32(2)

Docs.summary: Mismatched pixels are red, tolerated selected-channel differences amber (255,200,0), exact selected-channel matches dimmed actual RGB, and ignored pixels neutral gray (128,128,128).
Docs.remarks: The actual image is the second input. Exact-match RGB channels are divided by four, regardless of channel selection and without flattening transparency. Output alpha is always 255.

MemberSignature.Value: .field public static literal valuetype SkiaSharp.Testing.SKDifferenceStyle ThresholdOverlay = int32(3)

Docs.summary: Mismatched pixels are tinted red, tolerated selected-channel differences amber (255,200,0), and ignored pixels neutral gray (128,128,128), each blended at 50% over the actual image; exact selected-channel matches retain the actual image.
Docs.remarks: The actual image is the second input, flattened onto white before blending. All RGB channels remain visible regardless of channel selection. Half-channel values round upward and output alpha is always 255.
